openings.name: Italian Game (Giuoco Piano)
openings.intro: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 — White develops quickly and aims the bishop at the weak f7 square. The Italian is one of the oldest openings: direct, principled, and rich in tactics.
openings.traps: Variants & traps: 3...Bc5 leads to the quiet Giuoco Piano; 3...Be7 is the Two Knights Defence territory. Trap: after 4.c3 Nf6 5.d4 exd4 6.cxd4?? Bb4+ wins material — take with 6.e5! instead. Black can also play the sharp 3...d6 (Hungarian).

openings.name: Ruy Lopez (Spanish Opening)
openings.intro: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 — the Spanish Opening: White pins the knight and keeps long-term pressure on e5 without committing pawns. The most popular opening at master level for 500 years.
openings.traps: Variants & traps: 3...a6 4.Ba4 Nf6 is the main line (Berlin 4...d6 and Marshall 4...Nf6 are famous sub-variants). Trap: the Open Ruy (5.d4) is double-edged; Black's ...Bb4+ pin tricks and the Exchange variation (4.Bxc6) are quieter but solid.

openings.name: Scotch Game
openings.intro: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.d4 — White strikes the center immediately and avoids the deep theory of the Italian. After 3...exd4 White usually recaptures with the knight (3...d6 allows 4.d5).
openings.traps: Variants & traps: 4.Nxd4 Bc5 5.Nb3 (the 'Scotch Gambit' 5.c3!? is risky but fun); 4...Nf6 5.Nc3 is the main line. Trap: 4.d5?! Nxd5? no — after 3...exd4 4.d5?? Nxd5 5.Nxd5 Qxd5 loses the queen-side development race.

openings.name: Evans Gambit
openings.intro: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Bc5 4.b4 — White sacrifices a pawn for rapid development and open lines against f7. Romantic, tactical, and still dangerous at every level.
openings.traps: Variants & traps: 4...Bxb4 5.c3 is the accepted Evans; 5...Ba5 6.d4 exd4 is the main line. Trap: the 'Compromised Defence' 5...Bc5?! 6.bxc5 d6 7.Bb5+ looks scary for Black but 7...Nfd7 defends; White's 6.e5!? is the sharp try.

openings.name: King's Gambit
openings.intro: 1.e4 e5 2.f4 — the King's Gambit: White sacrifices a pawn for a fast attack on f7. The most romantic opening in chess.
openings.traps: Variants & traps: 2...exf4 is forced; after 3.Nf3 g5 4.Bc4 g4 5.O-O Black must defend accurately (5...Qg5?! loses to 6.Ne5). Trap: 3.d4 (declined) is solid; the 'Cunningham' 3.Bc4 is unsound but tricky.

openings.name: Vienna Game
openings.intro: 1.e4 e5 2.Nc3 — the Vienna Game: White prepares f4 (a mini King's Gambit) while keeping the knight flexible.
openings.traps: Variants & traps: 2...Nf6 3.f4 is the main Vienna; 3...Bc5 4.f4 exf4 transposes to the King's Gambit. Trap: after 3.f4 exf4 4.d4 Qh4+ 5.Ke2 the king walk is dangerous for White — 5...d5! 6.exd5 Bg4+ is fine for Black.

openings.name: Philidor Defence
openings.intro: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 d6 — Black defends e5 solidly with the pawn, a classical, compact setup.
openings.traps: Variants & traps: 3.d4 exd4 4.Nxd4 Nf6 5.Nc3 is the main line (the 'Lion' 3...g6 is a modern try). Trap: 3.Nc3?! Nf6 4.d4 exd4 5.Nxd4 Nxe4?? loses to 6.Qxd8+ — but Black simply plays 5...c6.

openings.name: French Defence
openings.intro: 1.e4 e6 — the French Defence: Black builds a solid pawn chain (d5) and counter-attacks on the queenside or the center. Black's most popular answer to 1.e4.

openings.name: Sicilian Defence
openings.intro: 1.e4 c5 — the Sicilian: Black fights asymmetrically for the d4 square and the queenside, leading to the richest opening complex in chess.
openings.traps: Variants & traps: 2.Nf3 d6 (Najdorf/Dragon/Scheveningen territory), 2...e6 (Kan/Taimanov), 2...Nc6 (Classical). openings.name: Semi-Slav Defence
openings.intro: 1.d4 d5 2.c4 c6 3.Nf3 Nf6 4.Nc3 e6 — the Semi-Slav: Slav structure with the ...e6 bishop active. Sharp and popular at elite level.
openings.traps: Variants & traps: 5.e3 Nbd7 6.Bd3 dxc4 7.Bxc4 b5 is the main Meran/Anti-Moscow territory. Trap: 6.Bd3?! dxc4 7.Bxc4 b5 8.Be2 Bb7 9.O-O b4!? 10.Na4 c5! 11.dxc5 Nxc5 wins a piece — the famous Botvinnik trap.

openings.name: King's Indian Defence
openings.intro: 1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 g6 — the King's Indian: Black fianchettos and counter-attacks e4/e5 with ...e5 or ...c5. One of the most fighting defences.
openings.traps: Variants & traps: 3.Nc3 Bg7 4.e4 d6 5.Nf3 O-O 6.Be2 e5 (mainline Mar del Plata) — the Sämisch 4...O-O 5.f3 c5 6.e4 Nc6 is critical. Trap: in the Classical, 7.O-O Nc6 8.d5 Ne5?! 9.Nxe5! dxe5 10.Qxd8 wins — Black must play 8...Na5.

openings.name: Nimzo-Indian Defence
openings.intro: 1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Bb4 — the Nimzo-Indian: Black pins the knight to double White's pawns, the strategically deepest defence to 1.d4.
openings.traps: Variants & traps: 4.e3 O-O 5.Bd3 d5 6.Nf3 c5 7.O-O dxc4 8.Bxc4 Nbd7; the Rubinstein 4.Qc2 is the main alternative. Trap: 4.e3 O-O 5.Bd3 d5 6.Nf3 c5 7.O-O dxc4 8.Bxc4 cxd4?! 9.exd4 Nc6 10.Bg5 and White regains the pawn with pressure — play 8...b5! instead.

openings.name: Queen's Indian Defence
openings.intro: 1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 e6 3.Nf3 b6 — the Queen's Indian: Black fianchettos the bishop to b7 and plays ...d5 later. Solid and hypermodern.
openings.traps: Variants & traps: 4.g3 Ba6 (or 4...Bb7 mainline) 5.b3 d5 6.Bg2 Be7 7.O-O O-O; the Kasparov 4.g3 Ba6 5.b3 b6 is sharp. Trap: 4.Nc3 Bb7 5.Bg5 h6 6.Bh4 g5 7.Bg3 Ne4 — the 'Queen's Indian trap' — 8.Qc2! f5 9.e3 wins the piece back.

openings.name: Grünfeld Defence
openings.intro: 1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 g6 3.Nc3 d5 — the Grünfeld: Black attacks the big center with ...dxc4 and ...Bg7 pressure. Dynamic and popular at top level.
openings.traps: Variants & traps: 4.cxd5 Nxd5 5.e4 Nxc3 6.bxc3 Bg7 7.Bc4 (or 7.Nf3) — the Russian System 5...Nxc3 6.bxc3 c5 is mainline. Trap: 4.Nf3 Bg7 5.cxd5 O-O 6.e4 Nxd5 7.Nxd5 exd5?? no — 4.cxd5 Nxd5 5.e4 Nxc3 6.bxc3 Bg7 7.Bc4 O-O 8.Nf3 and White has a lasting center.

openings.name: London System
openings.intro: 1.d4 d5 2.Bf4 (or 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.Bf4) — the London System: a simple, repeatable setup with Bf4, e3, Nbd2, c3, O-O. Popular at all levels.
openings.traps: Variants & traps: 2...Nf6 3.Nf3 e6 4.e3 c5 5.c3 Nc6 6.Bd3 Bd6 is the main line; Black can play 2...Bf5!? or the sharp 2...c5. Trap: 4...Bd6 5.Nbd2 O-O 6.e3 e5?! 7.dxe5 Nxe5 8.Nxe5 Bxe5?? loses to 9.Nxe5 — careful with ...e5 breaks.

openings.name: English Opening
openings.intro: 1.c4 — the English Opening: White controls d5 from the flank and often transposes to d4 or Réti structures. Positional and flexible.
openings.traps: Variants & traps: 1...e5 (Reversed Sicilian) 2.Nc3 Nf6 3.Nf3 Nc6 4.g3 d5 is critical; 1...c5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 is the Symmetrical English. Trap: 1...e5 2.Nc3 Nf6 3.Nf3 Nc6 4.e3?! d5 5.d4 exd4 6.exd4?? d4! wins a piece — play 4.g3 instead.
